supported_claims.text: Evidence supports competing interpretations of the early form: a picture of opposed wings, or Wang Qingju’s proposal that it shows two people back-to-back. Neither interpretation is settled by the supplied graphic evidence.

The received Shuowen account interprets 非 as opposition and explains the form as the lower wings of 飛 facing away from one another. This is a historical interpretation, not independent proof of the graph’s origin or a dated path to negation.

Reported oracle-bone examples already use 非 as a negative, and the sources also report a possible place-name use. The earliest script class in the dossier is oracle-bone, but it does not establish an absolute date or prove that negation developed from wings or opposition.

Later reported uses include faults or judging something wrong, as well as reproach, slander, and avoid. The supplied evidence does not establish a complete chronology or semantic chain among these uses.
The proposal that the spoken word 非 arose through fusion of 不 and 惟 is disputed. It concerns lexical and phonological history; it does not show that the graph is composed of 不 and 惟.
The selected historical glyph is a modern vector redraw in Shang oracle-script style, associated with a Xiaoxuetang record; it is not an ancient artifact photograph.

disagreements.text: The early graphic form is interpreted either as opposed wings, following the received Shuowen explanation and related accounts, or as two people back-to-back in Wang Qingju’s proposal. The dossier does not resolve the competing readings.

A proposed relation to 北 is advanced by Wang Qingju, while another discussion says the graph evidence does not establish a shared origin with 飛 and does not independently verify the 北 analysis. The original referent remains unresolved.
The 不 + 惟 fusion is reported as a debated account of the spoken word. The sources discuss differing reconstructions and sound-change proposals; the dossier does not establish the fusion as fact.

limitations.text: The reported early negative examples do not establish whether negation developed from an earlier pictorial or opposition sense; no dated semantic sequence is supported.
The listed later senses and examples do not establish a full chronology or the semantic links among opposition, wrongness, reproach, and negation.

No proposed phonetic component in 非’s own graphic formation is established in the inspected analyses. Character readings and reconstructions therefore do not support assigning a phonetic component or component-level sound comparison.
No glyph image was visually inspected in the research. The selected illustration is a modern redraw, and the exact underlying database image was not separately retrieved.
